correctness.rationale: For n<=k the length-n count identifies the word. Otherwise, the count of a (k-1)-factor minus its left-extended k-factor counts picks out the unique prefix, with the empty prefix used at k=1; reversal fixes the suffix. A length j<=k of the same parity as n has one centered start. Reversal pairs every other occurrence of a palindromic factor at this length and fixes the center, so the unique odd-multiplicity palindromic j-factor is the central word. Take the largest such j, allowing j=0; for n<=3k the central start is at most k, since n<=3k-1 when n has parity opposite k. With the (k-1)-prefix and its mirror already known, the only possible gap is one distinct mirrored pair, identifiable by subtracting known letters from the singleton counts. The argument covers overlaps and k=1; it uses ordinary palindromicity of both candidate words, not palindromicity up to equivalence. In each boundary witness every marker is at least k-1 positions from both ends and the two markers are at least k apart, so each one-marker word of length j<=k occurs twice at its specified offset and the all-zero count is 3k+2-3j. The witnesses have distinct first-marker positions and are ordinary palindromes, giving sharpness over any alphabet with two letters. A separate enumeration generated palindromes from their first halves and compared full factor profiles in 82 finite (alphabet size, order, length) slices (binary k<=5, ternary k<=3, four-letter k<=2), and checked the supplied witnesses for k<=20; the source scripts were inspected but not executed. The universal conclusion rests on the symbolic proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The unrestricted theorem rules out shorter collisions and settles the structure at length 2k, but it does not classify palindrome collisions at subsequent lengths or force injectivity through 3k; the reversal-center argument is additional.

originality.rationale: The generic k-Abelian framework and the prior order-three case are covered and not credited as new. The all-order sharp threshold for reversal-fixed words, with the parity-based constructive argument, is not supplied by the inspected equivalence, shortest-collision or rich/poor results. This is a bounded assessment, with explicitly unresolved access to portions of the related literature.
residual_risks: The complete DLT 2014 and 2018 Information and Computation articles were not independently obtained; the accessible presentation is not a substitute for checking every assertion in those papers.

On the Multiset of Factors of a String was a search lead whose OA retrieval returned 403; lack of access is not an exclusion. Unindexed results phrased as reversal-fixed reconstruction remain possible.

value.rationale: The occurrence profile is a standard string invariant and reflection symmetry is a natural source restriction. The uniform theorem measures exactly how much symmetry improves the first loss of information, and the parity-of-center decoder provides a structural explanation rather than an order-three recomputation. The binary witness hits the bound at every order. The claim does not solve the unrestricted reconstruction problem or classify all fibers above the threshold.
